note: Generated by wave_stream_contract.py emit. Do not hand-edit: fixtures/*.json is the source, *.mp is the compiled wire form, and `emit --check` proves they agree.

fixtures.name: reject_annotation_channel_ref
fixtures.why: An annotation anchored to a channel HELO never declared (ERR ANNOTATION_REF). The consumer has no row for it, so the event is decoded correctly and then dropped on the floor.

fixtures.name: reject_annotation_ts_inverted
fixtures.why: ts_end before ts_start. A negative-width span is not a rendering curiosity: the consumer places decoded frames on a timeline by this pair.

fixtures.name: reject_channel_total_bits
fixtures.why: channel_total_bits disagrees with the sum of the channel widths. The consumer slices every SAMPLES value by this number, so a wrong total does not fail — it silently decodes every channel off by the difference.

fixtures.name: reject_duplicate_channel_id
fixtures.why: Two channels share an id. Ids are the consumer's only handle for routing annotations to rows, so a duplicate quietly merges two buses into one lane.

fixtures.name: reject_edge_anchor_missing
fixtures.why: EDGE_EVENTS words with no anchor_ns in a session that also carries absolutely-timestamped annotations. A word holds only the LOW 16 BITS of its microsecond timestamp, so the edges are placeable only inside a 65.536 ms window; mixed with annotation time they land a whole board uptime away — measured at 10 days (LT-P2.105), which is how the edge lanes held thousands of transitions and drew nothing.

fixtures.name: reject_edge_lane_on_sample_channel
fixtures.why: A SAMPLES channel (level_pin[2], width 1) sits at id 2 while the session's EDGE_EVENTS words carry device_id 2. A consumer names the edge lane of device_id 2 after the HELO channel with that id, so the edge lane either takes the sample lane's name or cannot be named: the DS-P3.124 defect, where level_pin[1]/[2] at ids 1/2 left the I2C edge lanes as edge_1/edge_2.

fixtures.name: reject_event_id_names_two_events
fixtures.why: Two different annotations under one event_id. An HWTX verdict points at the event it judges by this id, so once the id names two events every such reference is ambiguous and the verdict lands on whichever one the reader finds first. Sending the SAME event again under its id is legal (a keyframe does it); naming a second event is not.

fixtures.name: reject_frame_after_eof
fixtures.why: A frame after EOF. EOF means flush and close; a producer that keeps sending leaves the consumer unable to tell a finished capture from a stalled one.

fixtures.name: reject_loss_unknown_stage
fixtures.why: A loss annotation naming a stage outside the provenance taxonomy. The point of the taxonomy is that a loss is attributable to a pipeline stage; an unknown stage is exactly the unattributable number it replaced.

fixtures.name: reject_missing_annotation_text
fixtures.why: An annotation with no text. text is REQUIRED — it is the label the consumer draws inline on the waveform, so an annotation without one is an event the user cannot see.

fixtures.name: reject_no_helo
fixtures.why: Data before the handshake. Without HELO the consumer has no channel descriptors, so every annotation it receives is unplaceable — and a producer that streams anyway looks 'alive' while showing nothing.

fixtures.name: reject_not_a_frame
fixtures.why: A one-element array on the wire. Every frame is [tag, payload]; anything else is FRAME_DECODE, and a consumer must report it rather than index into whatever it got.

fixtures.name: reject_payload_role_key
fixtures.why: An i2c_byte annotation whose payload is keyed 'value' instead of the contracted 'data'. The consumer builds its per-protocol packet columns from these keys, so a renamed role key empties a column instead of raising anything — the quietest possible cross-repo break.

fixtures.name: reject_samples_ts_regress
fixtures.why: SAMPLES timestamps run backwards inside one frame. The consumer appends transitions streaming-wise; a backwards ts corrupts the waveform rather than reordering it.

fixtures.name: reject_seq_regress
fixtures.why: ANNOTATIONS seq goes backwards. seq exists so a consumer can detect drops by its gaps; a non-monotonic seq turns that detector into noise.

fixtures.name: reject_stats_proto_set_changes
fixtures.why: The wire-observable half of DS-P3.120's 'a live data logger reports nothing': the proto_stats key set changes within one session — jtag is present in the first STATS and gone from the second. A build's data-logger set is fixed for its lifetime, so the viewer sees a row vanish under it while the data logger is still live.

fixtures.name: reject_stats_stale_proto_set
fixtures.why: The DS-P3.120 defect, reproduced: STATS.proto_stats keyed by a hardcoded list that still carries a retired i2s datalogger and has lost the live can and jtag ones. The consumer renders one row per key, so this ships a phantom row for a datalogger that does not exist while two real buses report nothing at all.

fixtures.name: reject_tag_body_collision
fixtures.why: The D.14 defect, reproduced: a frame tagged 9 (SYNC) carrying an EDGE_EVENTS body. This is what two repos independently assigning a tag looks like on the wire, and it is why the required-key set — not the tolerated extra keys — is what makes a body belong to its tag.

fixtures.name: reject_text_res_missing_long
fixtures.why: A text_res with no long resolution. A reader that asks for the long label of an event gets nothing, so text_res carries both resolutions or is left out.

fixtures.name: reject_text_res_short_too_long
fixtures.why: A text_res.short longer than the 32-character inline label. The short resolution exists to fit on the waveform and in a tight token budget; a short label that is as long as the long one gives the reader no choice at all.

fixtures.name: reject_truncated_frame
fixtures.why: The last frame is cut short — what a dropped connection or a killed producer actually leaves in the buffer. The trailing bytes are not a frame, and treating a partial map as a whole one is how half a STATS snapshot gets rendered as truth.

fixtures.name: reject_unregistered_channel_enum
fixtures.why: A channel descriptor uses type 'Annotation' and radix 'Decimal' — neither is a registered member. The consumer does not fail on these: it falls back to Signal/Hexadecimal, so the producer's intent is dropped and NOBODY is told. That silence is why the contract checks the members on the producer side.

fixtures.name: reject_version_mismatch
fixtures.why: HELO.ver names a wire version this side does not implement. This is the ONE fatal incompatibility in the policy: the consumer answers ERR VERSION_MISMATCH and closes rather than guessing at an unknown wire.

fixtures.name: reject_wrong_direction
fixtures.why: STATS on the consumer-to-producer stream. Direction is part of each tag's definition; a frame arriving from the wrong end means one side has the tag's role backwards, which is the same failure mode as a tag collision with a nicer disguise.

fixtures.name: session_datalogger_subset
fixtures.why: DS-P1.61: a build that does not carry every registered data logger. Since DS-P2.121 made the CAN data logger opt-in, the live daemon streams proto_stats keyed edge/i2c/jtag/spi/uart — no can. That is an honest build, not a stale one: the key set is a per-build selection from the registered vocabulary, stable across the session. A contract that pins one build's selection rejects every other build (RW-WS1 rejected exactly this live PolarFire stream, verdict=reject field=proto_stats).

fixtures.name: session_edge_lane_names
fixtures.why: Edge lanes named in HELO (2.8.0, DS-P3.124): the entries at ids 1 and 2 equal the device_ids of the EDGE_EVENTS words and have width 0, so a consumer labels those lanes i2c_scl and i2c_sda instead of edge_1 and edge_2. The SAMPLES channels stay above id 31.

fixtures.name: session_golden
fixtures.why: One conformant session covering everything the golden path depends on: the HELO/HELO_OK handshake and its channel-descriptor negotiation, one SAMPLES batch with monotonic timestamps, the catch-up SYNC boundary, decoded annotations for EVERY protocol targets/canfd_demo.yml captures (CAN incl. an error event, UART incl. a 9-bit char and a status error, I2C with ACK and NACK, SPI MOSI/MISO pairing, JTAG IR shift and TAP state), raw EDGE_EVENTS carrying BOTH a packed batch and legacy words with the absolute anchor_ns that makes them placeable, the loss counters in both provenance flavours (precise in-band and synthesized out-of-band) plus an error_run storm collapse, the edge_maxfreq max-frequency datum of a captured line both measured and as the re-armed null sentinel, a STATS frame with the full counter set including the nulls that mean 'no regbank slot', a DIGEST with a CRITICAL verdict, the CONTROL / CONTROL_ACK back-channel, a RATE_HINT, an UNKNOWN tag that MUST be skipped without ending the session, and a graceful EOF. Annotations carry the HWTX event_id and text_res {long, short}; a long label shows the short resolution clipped to 32 characters, one annotation goes without either key because both are optional, and one event is sent a second time under its own event_id, as a late joiner's keyframe resends it.
